projectSummary: This is the closest longitudinal programme-level analogue to the press-versus-fly question that this pass retrieved, and every axis of it is indirect. The contrast is whole programmes rather than two chest exercises; the chest single-joint work is a pec deck and an incline dumbbell fly, not a cable fly; the only upper-body outcome is 1RM bench press, which the multi-joint group practised and the single-joint group did not; and no pectoralis size measure was taken. The task-specificity qualifier is mandatory here.

publication.statusSource: Crossref REST API works record plus the Crossref/Retraction Watch CSV export, both fetched 2026-09-13

notes: The tier-2 outcome is the exercise one group trained, so the between-group difference confounds adaptation with practice of the test.
No pectoralis-specific size or strength outcome, so the study cannot bear on tier 1 at all.
Participants were soccer players in pre-season performing an identical concurrent soccer routine, which adds an unmeasured common exposure.
Baseline height differed between groups by about 3 cm, and randomisation is described but not detailed.

study.population: Thirty-six young male amateur soccer players with no previous resistance-training experience completed 4 weeks of familiarisation and were then randomly assigned to a single-joint group (n = 18; age 23.5 (SD 2.7) years, height 182.1 (SD 5.2) cm) or a multi-joint group (n = 18; age 25.5 (SD 3.8) years, height 185.3 (SD 3.6) cm) for 8 weeks, 3 sessions per week.

title: Resistance Training with Single vs. Multi-joint Exercises at Equal Total Load Volume: Effects on Body Composition, Cardiorespiratory Fitness, and Muscle Strength.
